assign.request: do we have user interfaces built out for that yet? And how would that look? I know we have demo apps where we can see the URL changing and click through different workflows. We really need to lean into that system to document these systems. creating a grid of user interface cards and each one represents a specific workflow like registration. I'd like to be able to study the user experience from landing page to sign up, how many clicks it takes to get logged in. using Google sign in has always been an objective of mine. I'd actually lean away from a third-party auth provider — raw APIs are almost always better than an aggregate API that shields you from the underlying API. social login — how to use those APIs to pull people's avatar image, or maybe look for a Gravatar.

decision.about: How the six workflow cards should talk to Google/GitHub: raw provider OAuth endpoints, or a third-party auth aggregator (Auth0/Clerk/Supabase)

options.say: Raw GitHub + Google OAuth, state + PKCE on both
options.why: Matches the owner's own words and /imagine/platform/decisions/identity.md ruling 1; no vendor domain in the login flow, no webhook-sync problem to keep profiles honest
Wins when a project needs many providers, MFA and compliance from day one — none of which this wall needs

decision.because: The owner said it outright ("having the raw APIs is almost always better than an aggregate API that shields you from the underlying API"), and it matches the platform's own already-ruled identity.md — nothing here re-argues that ruling, it just builds the UI on top of it.

log.msg: click counts measured live via headless Playwright against the own dev server (PORT=8125): (a) email signup 2, (b) Google 2, (c) GitHub 2, (d) returning sign-in 2, (e) sign out 1. Flow (b) shot at /imagine/platform/workflows/ logged-in state matches the counter exactly (2 clicks made, counter reads 2).

ux/Auth gap (consumed, not edited): login()/signup() always draw the social row and the Forgot-password link, no config word to hide either, only the social_row()/password_field() seams. FlowAuth.hideSocial must arrive in the CONSTRUCTOR ({view, hideSocial:true}), not as a property set after `new FlowAuth(...)` returns — Auth's own constructor builds the form synchronously, social row included, before any later line can run. First version set it after construction and silently shipped the social row anyway; caught by reading the render order, fixed before any screenshot.

layout: --column set in rem (20rem), not em, per the layout skill's columns-host warning (/imagine/platform/ is a COLUMN, width: large, ~535px at 1280 / ~1152px at 3440). Measured: 2 cards per row at 1920, 1 per row at 1400 — wraps to a single column rather than overflowing.

zero new CSS: every class used across flows.js/page.js is an existing framework.css utility (flex, v, gap, wrap, grid, auto, surface, pad, muted, h4, prim) — no new-css-class namespace opened, css-scopes.txt untouched.

assign.outcome:
**Six workflow cards landed on one wall — each a real `demo.app()` you can click through, with a live click counter that matches the clicks actually made.**

- [/imagine/platform/workflows/](/imagine/platform/workflows/) — the wall: sign up with email, Google sign-in, GitHub sign-in, returning-user sign-in, sign out, and a sixth card comparing a provider avatar to a real Gravatar
- [doc/decisions.md](/imagine/platform/workflows/doc/decisions.md) — the click counts, the real Google/GitHub endpoints cited, the provider-vs-aggregator call
- Source: [flows.js](/imagine/platform/workflows/flows.js) (the five trees), [page.js](/imagine/platform/workflows/page.js) (the wall)

**Click counts, measured live (headless, not designed-in):** sign up with email 2 · Google 2 · GitHub 2 · returning sign-in 2 · sign out 1.

![the wall at 1920, two cards per row inside the platform column](wall-1920.png)

**Left, and why:** no back/retry buttons inside a flow, so the counter never has to answer "does going back un-count a click" — a reader can still explore via the box's own breadcrumb urls. No real OAuth popup or account chooser — the brief rules that out; a mocked consent screen stands in, with the real request shown on the card's fold instead. Password reset stays reachable through ux/Auth's own "Forgot password?" link (not hidden — it's real, working behavior) but does not advance the counter, since the owner ruled it out as a seventh card.
